headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no documented shared channel, but mem0’s memory role could amplify bad inputs if connected.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing repo with no I/O surfaces or runnable agent behavior, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs. Profile B is a memory system, which could store or replay content if integrated, but no shared channel is documented. The pairwise pathway is therefore only plausible via unusual manual or external wiring.
conditions: IF an operator wires B’s stored text into A’s prompt or editor context
IF a shared clipboard, file, or MCP bridge is added between A and B
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Disable any automatic prompt replay from B into A
Review copied text before pasting into A
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to B outputs
requires-engineering: add a trust boundary between memory and prompt inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and exposes no filesystem or network surface, while B explicitly has network egress set to none. With no shared workspace or authenticated principal documented, there is no default leakage path. Any leakage would require an external integration that is not present in the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted access to the same workspace or files
IF B is reconfigured to export memory contents to another service
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared folder
Confirm B remains network-isolated
Use separate OS accounts for A and B
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs
requires-engineering: add audit logs for any export path

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no declared write, network, or concurrency capabilities, and B only declares network egress none. Without overlapping mutable-resource access, there is no plausible write-write or coordination conflict in the documented configuration. The pair is effectively non-overlapping on capabilities.
conditions: IF A is later given filesystem or git write access
IF B is later granted write access to the same mutable resource
mitigations: Leave A read-only
Keep B network-isolated
Avoid mounting the same writable directory
requires-engineering: add locking for shared resources
requires-engineering: define per-agent write scopes

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can generate prompt-engineering content that B might store or reuse as memory, but B is not documented as taking downstream actions and no direct action authority is shown. The main risk is mistaken reuse of A’s text as authoritative guidance if an operator connects them, which is a limited, indirect cascade.
conditions: IF B is configured to treat A’s text as authoritative memory
IF an operator uses B’s stored output as instructions without review
mitigations: Require human review before reuse
Label A output as untrusted reference material
Separate memory from instruction channels
requires-engineering: add verification gates before B reuses A output
requires-engineering: add source attribution to stored memories

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and A touches no data classes while B’s network egress is none. With no compliance-relevant data flow or mismatch evidenced, there is no documented compliance breach pathway in this pair.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later introduced into either agent
IF a deployment policy assigns different retention or residency rules to the same data
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through this pair
Document retention settings before deployment
Keep both agents out of PHI/PII workflows
requires-engineering: publish residency and retention controls
requires-engineering: add compliance review to integration approval
